notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity sizing and a precise latency SLO definition. Key ask: unambiguous measurement alignment (server-side vs client-side), and streaming vs non-streaming semantics.

SLO targets discussed (initial): p50=35-50ms non-streaming (short prompts), p95=120ms, p99<=350ms. For streaming (chat) they want initial token p95<80ms and per-chunk p95<40ms after stream established.

Measurement alignment issues: our engineers saw large variance between client-side wall-clock and Redwood-provided server timestamps. Causes called out: DNS/TCP/TLS handshake measured on client for first request, clock skew on load generators, client batching of responses, and differing definitions of "response complete" (server-end-of-stream vs client-assembled JSON). Customer explicitly: "We need a single source of truth for p99 — can't have vendor and client disagreeing."

Requested deliverables from Redwood: (1) server-side timing traces (receipt -> dispatch -> token emit), (2) streaming chunk latency definition + per-chunk timing instrumentation, (3) test harness configs and A/B scripts (deterministic seed prompts), (4) recommended reserved GPU footprint (equivalent to 8x A100-80GB for sustained 200RPS with KV cache) and clear oversubscription policies, (5) suggested SLA credit table for misses at p99 and p95 thresholds.

Throughput/Capacity notes: baseline workload = mixed chat + rerank with average token-length 220; working target sustained = 200 req/s, burst to 1k req/s for 2-5 minutes. They want deterministic guarantees (no more than X% falls below p95) during reserved windows. Planning conversation: prefer dedicated racks with pinned capacity, optional autoscale for burst but with defined cold-start behavior.

SLA negotiation points: financial credits for p99 misses (sliding scale), scheduled maintenance windows that are small and announced, regional residency (us-east fallback), per-route SLOs (feeding trade-alert route stricter than background summarization), and clear escalation path (SE -> AE -> SLT).

Current blockers: legal redlines, outstanding server-side traces from Redwood infra team, and inconsistent perf numbers from their internal load generator (time sync + instrumentation). Next step: joint test on 2025-03-05 to collect server-side traces and produce a reconciled SLO doc for legal to review.
